summary: Chana mushroom masala: tempered mustard, fennel, cumin and coriander seeds, a browned tomato mixture and chickpeas with mushrooms and spices simmered about 15 minutes, finished with tempered mustard seeds; 30 minutes with already-cooked chickpeas.
glance: 2 with just rice or 4 as part of a larger Indian meal
about 15 minutes, uncovered, until the sauce thickens
faq: Can I use canned chickpeas?

Yes. Canned chickpeas are often undercooked and a little crunchy, so drain and rinse them and simmer them in water to cover (or microwave them) while you prepare everything else. Skip this if they're already pleasantly soft.
How do I organize all the spices?
Gather the spice mixture in a small bowl, the tomato mixture in a medium bowl and the chickpea mixture in a medium bowl before you start cooking.
What is tempering?
Frying mustard seeds in a separate skillet in hot oil for just a few seconds until they pop and tossing them over the finished dish, a great way to add a final layer of flavor.
Can I leave out the mushrooms?
Yes. They add a little textural counterpoint without being a main focus, so you can omit them or use a different vegetable.
How thick should it be?
Cook uncovered over medium-low heat about 15 minutes, until the sauce begins to thicken, starting with about a cup of water so it is somewhat soupy; finish to the texture you want.

summary: Ginger and black pepper rice pilaf: a quick ghee, butter or oil seasoning of grated ginger, cumin, cinnamon and cayenne cooked 30 seconds, mixed with freshly ground pepper and folded into 6 cups of cooked basmati rice; serves 4 as a side.
glance: 1 packed tablespoon grated fresh ginger, cooked 30 seconds in 1/4 cup ghee, butter or oil
Vegetarian, gluten-free and kosher; vegan with oil
faq: Why is this pilaf made in an unusual way?
None of the flavorings are cooked in with the rice. You flavor the ghee, butter or oil with the seasonings and fold them into the cooked rice.
Do I need to peel the ginger?
No. Grated on a microplane the ginger is cut so finely that the skin becomes unnoticeable. Use fresh ginger and don't substitute powdered ginger.
Does the black pepper matter?
Yes. Use freshly ground pepper: when you grind it, the floral aromatic notes dissipate quickly, and pre-ground pepper is missing most of the goodness.
Can I make it as fried rice?
Yes. Prepare the seasoning in a larger skillet, add cooked and cooled basmati and stir-fry until tender.
Can I use another rice?
Another long-grain rice would still be good, but not short-grain or sticky rice.
How do I turn it into a one-dish meal?
Add cooked chickpeas (about a third of the volume of rice) and serve with Indian lime pickle and yogurt.

summary: Saffron chickpea stew with grilled porcini: porcini roasted in foil packets at 450°F until tender (about 30 minutes), then grilled; chickpeas simmered about 15 minutes in a sauce of onion, tomato paste, garlic, saffron, smoked paprika and a cup of dry white wine.
glance: about 20 ounces; foil-roast at 450°F (about 30 minutes), then grill on a hot grill pan
simmer about 15 minutes; chickpeas 5 cups cooked
can be made a day ahead; the flavors improve
faq: Can I make the stew without fresh porcini?
Yes, it is well worth making anyway. Serve it with sauteed morels or crimini (don't roast and grill those), or take it in a different direction over couscous.
What is the best way to cook porcini?

The author's favorite: roast them in a foil packet until tender but not overly soft, then grill them for grill marks and a lightly caramelized surface, rather than cooking them until limp and steamed.
What wine should I use?
Something drinkable, since a full cup goes in the sauce and you'll taste it. The author used a very dry Riesling because it was open; a Spanish red would also be great.
Can I make it ahead?
Yes. The stew can be made a day ahead, and the lusty flavors of wine, garlic and saffron only get better with time.
How do I check if vegetables are tender?
A cake tester pokes a mushroom, artichoke or potato leaving an imperceptibly small hole, and cooks in fine-dining kitchens carry them in their jacket pockets.
What do I serve with the stew?
A green salad and grilled bread, made by brushing artisan bread with olive oil and toasting it or pressing it on the grill pan.

summary: Cooked carrot and radish salad: small, sweet carrots boiled in well-salted water until just tender and shocked in ice water, tossed with an unemulsified lime or lemon and ginger olive oil dressing and thin-sliced colorful radishes, finished with dill and finishing salt.
glance: 1 bunch small, sweet carrots with tops, boiled until just tender and shocked in ice water
1/2 cup olive oil, 1/4 cup lime or lemon juice, 1 teaspoon grated ginger
faq: How do you boil carrots for a salad?

Use a good-sized pot of well-salted water at a full boil, check the carrots frequently for tenderness, and the very second they're done plunge them into ice water to stop the cooking and preserve the texture and color.
Can I use other vegetables?
Baby beets, turnips or even potatoes would be just as wonderful. You could also add toasted sesame seeds or a pesto made from the carrot tops.
Why isn't the dressing emulsified?

After staging at Canlis, the author likes to intentionally not emulsify dressings, letting the oil separate for an attractive look on the plate. To emulsify, add a small amount of mustard or xanthan gum and whiz it just before serving, or whisk the oil in a thin stream.
What do I do with extra dressing?
The recipe makes more dressing than you need, and you can use it the next day in a different salad.
How do I trim the carrots?
Peel them and trim the tops, leaving about 1/2 inch of stem.

summary: Banana, buttermilk and brown sugar "triple B" muffins: the wet ingredients, including frozen or very ripe bananas and fresh ginger, blended in a blender, folded gently into the dry ingredients and baked at 375°F for about 25 minutes; makes 12 in 35 minutes.
glance: 375°F (convection if available) for about 25 minutes, until golden brown
faq: Why blend the wet ingredients?
The author mixed all the wet ingredients, including hard-frozen bananas, in a Vita-Mix, and the muffins came out tender with a moist, open crumb.
Do I need a powerful blender?
No. If you don't have a jet-powered blender, use unfrozen bananas or defrost frozen ones in the microwave first.
What bananas should I use?
Two very ripe, ideally overripe bananas. Freezing bananas that are in danger of getting too brown is a handy way to save them for baking or smoothies.
Can I leave out the ginger?
Yes, omit the fresh ginger or use 1/4 teaspoon of dried ginger for a more standard baking flavor.
How do I keep the muffins tender?
Stir as little as possible to avoid developing gluten, which would make them tough. An ice-cream scoop works well for filling the cups.

summary: Jicama, orange and radish salad: jicama batons, quartered radishes, valencia orange segments and cilantro tossed with salt, pepper and 1/4 cup of fresh orange juice as the only dressing; a quick, refreshing side for Mexican and Latin American meals.
glance: 1/2 jicama, peeled and cut into 1/4 x 1/4 x 2-inch batons
faq: What is jicama?

Pronounced hee-come-uh, a root with a texture crisp like an apple and a little sweet. The author has only used it in salads. It's surprisingly easy to find in the specialty section of fairly average grocery stores and at Mexican markets.
Why serve a salad like this with a rich entree?
A refreshing salad offers a nice contrast, makes the meal a little lighter and cuts the fattiness of the main dish. This one is good with Mexican and other Latin American meals.
How do I cut oranges into supremes?
Cut the segments free of the membrane, reserving the juice, which is the dressing here.
How is the salad dressed?
Only with fresh orange juice: toss the jicama, radishes, orange segments and cilantro with a big pinch of salt, several grinds of pepper and 1/4 cup of the orange juice, then taste and adjust.

summary: Sephardic-style breaded cauliflower, learned from Noni Sophie: microwaved florets tossed with flour, egg and more flour in one bowl, shallow-fried until golden, then simmered 10 minutes in a lemony tomato sauce; serves 4 as a side in 30 minutes.
glance: flour, egg wash, flour, tossed together in one bowl
10 minutes in the sauce, so the breading softens but doesn't melt away
faq: Why bread and fry cauliflower and then soak it in sauce?

It sounds like a bad idea, but the author says it totally works: the result is savory, toothsome and satisfying. You can also skip the sauce and serve the crispy breaded cauliflower with a sprinkle of sea salt.
How do I bread cauliflower with less mess?

Toss the florets with half the flour, salt and pepper in one bowl, then toss with the egg beaten with 2 tablespoons of water, then add the remaining flour and toss again, all in the same bowl. Use just enough flour that it sticks with very little excess left at the bottom.
How do I pre-cook the cauliflower?
Microwave the florets under pierced plastic wrap on high for about 4 minutes until just slightly tenderized, or boil in salted water for 1 minute and drain well. Cool to just warm before breading.
How long do I simmer the cauliflower in the sauce?
About ten minutes, so the breading softens but doesn't completely melt and float away. Add a little water if the sauce seems too thick.
How thick should the tomato sauce be?

Noni serves it with a thin sauce, so use tomato sauce or crushed tomatoes depending on the texture you want. The author didn't find it worked well over polenta with pesto, and thinks it's best as a side dish.

summary: Savory cardoon flan: cardoon stalks stringed, soaked 30 minutes and simmered about 30 minutes in cream, milk, garlic and Parmigiano, pureed, strained, mixed with 4 eggs and baked in ramekins in a water bath at 350°F for about 25 minutes; makes 4.
glance: 1/2 pound (about 2 stalks), soaked 30 minutes in salted lemon water
350°F in a water bath, about 25 minutes, until just set

summary: Chickpea and saffron pilaf with crispy onions: basmati rice sauteed in the flavorful oil left from frying onions, cooked covered about 20 minutes, then topped on one side with saffron water and folded with chickpeas, dill and mint; prep 30 minutes, cook 1 hour.
glance: 2 cups basmati, sauteed about 3 minutes in the onion oil, then 3 1/2 cups water
a big pinch in about 2 tablespoons boiling water, poured on one side of the pot
hot or at room temperature, with lemon wedges
faq: What is the secret of this pilaf?
Using the flavorful oil left over from making the crispy onions to saute the rice before adding any water, which adds a rich, savory background that makes the dish more satisfying.
How do restaurants make saffron rice with some grains tinted and others white?
It doesn't take two pots. Make the rice as usual, then drizzle a bit of saffron-infused water on one side of the pot and let it absorb before fluffing.
How do I cook the rice?

Saute the rice and salt in the hot onion oil about 3 minutes until translucent, add 3 1/2 cups water, cover and bring to a boil, then reduce to the barest simmer for about 20 minutes until all the water is absorbed.
Does the pilaf need to be served hot?
No. It works well for summer potlucks because it doesn't need to be served hot.
How do I serve it?
As a main course with a last-minute squeeze of lemon, or as a side in a larger Middle Eastern spread. Mound it on a platter and garnish with the remaining dill, mint, fried onions and flaky salt.

summary: Persimmon carpaccio with fennel salad: fuyu persimmons sliced 1 mm thick on a mandoline and cut into rounds, topped with a salad of shaved fennel, radish and red onion in olive oil, champagne vinegar and salt, with pepitas; ready in 10 minutes.
glance: 2-3 fuyu (the firm, squat kind, not hachiya), sliced about 1 mm thick
faq: What kinds of persimmon are there?

Two general types. Fuyu persimmons, short and squat like an orange tomato, are eaten while still firm. Hachiya persimmons can only be eaten when incredibly soft, nearly pudding, or they are inedibly astringent.
Can I use hachiya persimmons for carpaccio?
No. You'll have a frightful mess. Scoop hachiyas out with a spoon or make persimmon pudding.
How do I slice the persimmons?
About 1 mm thick on a mandoline, discarding the end slices, then use a circle cutter (2 1/2 inches was perfect) to cut out each slice. Without the cutter, peel the persimmons first.
How do I assemble the plates?

Chill four salad plates, arrange 7 persimmon slices in a circle on each, and top with a quarter of the dressed fennel, radish and onion salad, keeping it centered and tall. Garnish with fennel fronds and toasted pepitas.
